judged_text: The credential-sync endpoint becomes a hard, unguarded dependency of the token-refresh path: the fetch has no timeout, no response.ok check, and the design provides no fallback once the placeholder refresh token has replaced the real one. If the parent cal.com instance is slow or down, every calendar operation needing a refresh hangs (Node fetch has no default timeout) or fails with an HTML error page flowing into the token parsers — a cascading failure across all shared-credential apps with no degradation path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new token-refresh branch via `refreshOAuthTokens()` that, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, performs a bare `fetch()` to the sync endpoint and returns the raw `Response` without any `response.ok` check or JSON parsing, and with no timeout (Node fetch has none by default): `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`. Several call sites expect non-`Response` shapes (e.g., HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object; Zoho expects an Axios response with `.data`; Google expects `res.data`), so the shared-credential path can break at runtime. Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` forcibly injects a dummy refresh token when missing (`refresh_token = "refresh_token"`), and Office365 then merges and persists that into the credential record (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which can overwrite the real refresh token and cause subsequent refreshes to fail with no fallback. These are concrete, diff-grounded correctness/availability defects.
